reading.stem: 다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks:
Dear Council Members,
The proposed timetable removes the 7:15 bus from Hill Road. The next service reaches school well after the first bell. Many parents on our street start work before seven, and the walking route crosses a highway without a footpath. The bus may appear quiet during the holidays, but its school-day passengers have no reasonable alternative. Please keep the early service in place and count its passengers during a full school week before making a final decision. I would be happy to bring other residents to the transport meeting.
Sincerely, Ian Moss
choices: 학교 방학 동안의 도보 통학을 홍보하려고
등교 시간대 버스 운행을 유지하고 이용 실태를 다시 살펴 달라고 요청하려고
버스 정기권을 온라인으로 구매하는 법을 문의하려고
evidence: Please keep the early service in place and count its passengers during a full school week before making a final decision.
reading.explanation:
정답 ④ · 글의 목적
현 시간표의 첫 버스가 없어지면 학생들이 늦게 된다. 방학의 인상보다 실제 학기 중 이용자 수를 근거로 결정해 달라는 요청이다.
근거 “Please keep the early service in place and count its passengers during a full school week before making a final decision.”

reading.stem: 다음 글에 드러난 주인공의 심경 변화로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: A brass plate for the new supervisor's door lay on the desk, its lettering hidden by tissue paper. Leo had been invited to a private meeting just after the interviews. He imagined his name under the paper and thought about the first change he would make. The director asked him to sit. “I wanted you to hear it from me,” she began. “The position went to Anna.” His prepared words of thanks suddenly seemed absurd; he folded his hands to hide their trembling. Through the glass wall the empty office no longer seemed to belong to his future.
evidence: His prepared words of thanks suddenly seemed absurd; he folded his hands to hide their trembling.
reading.explanation:
정답 ⑤ · 심경 변화
승진할 것으로 기대해 감사 인사까지 준비했지만 다른 사람이 뽑혔다는 말을 듣고 충격과 실망을 느낀다.
근거 “His prepared words of thanks suddenly seemed absurd; he folded his hands to hide their trembling.”

reading.stem: 다음 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: A craft shop displayed a hand-printed poster for months without selling it. When the artist announced that the printing block had been retired, customers began asking about the remaining copies. The ink and paper had not improved. What changed was the possibility of postponing a decision. A seller should not invent a shortage that does not exist; that would destroy trust. But when a product genuinely cannot be replaced, buyers need that information as much as they need the price. Point out a real limit on availability so buyers can judge what waiting may cost them.
choices: 소비자가 문의하기 전까지는 생산 중단 사실을 숨겨야 한다.
판매를 늘리려면 공급이 충분해도 부족하다고 말해야 한다.
한정 수량 제품에는 가격 표시를 하지 않는 것이 낫다.
제품을 나중에 구하기 어려운 실제 이유가 있다면 구매자에게 알려야 한다.
재고가 줄면 제품의 물리적 품질이 나아진다고 설명해야 한다.
evidence: Point out a real limit on availability so buyers can judge what waiting may cost them.
reading.explanation:
정답 ④ · 필자의 주장
필자는 허위 희소성을 금하지만 생산 중단 같은 실제 한계는 기다릴 때 잃을 기회를 판단하는 데 필요하다고 한다.
근거 “Point out a real limit on availability so buyers can judge what waiting may cost them.”

reading.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>timetable for the digital postman</u>의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은? [3점]
blocks: If a phone buzzes only three times during a study period, its owner may still look at it thirty times. Each glance is an attempt to discover whether something has happened since the last one. The interruptions can therefore multiply without a single extra message. A student who establishes a <u>timetable for the digital postman</u> chooses two short periods for ordinary messages and closes the inbox between them. Important contacts can still be given a separate way to reach her. The point is to make routine checking predictable so attention can settle on the task in front of her.
choices: give up electronic communication in emergencies
set regular times to check ordinary electronic messages
employ another person to remove unwanted mail
schedule all study for the hour after midnight
answer every message as soon as its author sends it
evidence: The point is to make routine checking predictable so attention can settle on the task in front of her.
reading.explanation:
정답 ② · 함축 의미
디지털 우편배달부의 시간표는 메시지가 왔는지 수시로 확인하지 않고 확인 시간을 정해 집중을 보호하는 방식을 가리킨다.
근거 “The point is to make routine checking predictable so attention can settle on the task in front of her.”

reading.stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: A detective in a story finds a wallet on an empty train. Returning it would be predictable; throwing away the money and keeping a child's photograph makes us lean forward. The question is no longer simply what the detective has done. We want to know what sort of person would make that choice. Later scenes can answer part of the question while raising it again under greater pressure. The wallet itself may never appear again. A story holds attention when its events make readers curious about the person responding to them. The action gives that curiosity a place to begin.
choices: 등장인물의 성격을 처음에 모두 설명하면 호기심이 오래간다.
사건의 규모가 클수록 인물의 선택은 중요하지 않다.
인물의 행동이 그 사람에 대한 궁금증을 일으킬 때 이야기에 몰입하게 된다.
독자는 예상대로 움직이는 인물에게서 가장 큰 긴장을 느낀다.
사건의 물건은 이야기 끝까지 반드시 반복해서 등장해야 한다.
evidence: A story holds attention when its events make readers curious about the person responding to them.
reading.explanation:
정답 ③ · 글의 요지
사진만 가져가는 뜻밖의 행동은 ‘어떤 사람이기에?’라는 질문을 낳는다. 사건은 인물에 대한 궁금증을 일으키는 역할을 한다.
근거 “A story holds attention when its events make readers curious about the person responding to them.”

reading.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: Two people may blink the same number of times during a minute yet look quite different to an observer. One closes her eyelids slowly while listening; the other's eyes snap shut and open at the sound of a falling tray. Counting blinks alone erases that distinction. Changes in speed can add information about a person's response to the situation, especially when compared with the way the same person usually blinks. A single fast blink is no proof of a particular feeling. The timing of a movement can supply clues that its frequency alone leaves out.
choices: a method for measuring eyesight by counting blinks
why a falling object produces the same reaction in everyone
the use of blinking to conceal every sign of emotion
why slow movements are easier to count than quick ones
what blink speed can add to an observation of behavior
evidence: The timing of a movement can supply clues that its frequency alone leaves out.
reading.explanation:
정답 ⑤ · 글의 주제
횟수가 같은 눈 깜박임도 속도와 맥락에 따라 다르게 해석될 수 있다는 글이다. 한 동작을 감정의 확실한 증거라고 단정하지 않는다.
근거 “The timing of a movement can supply clues that its frequency alone leaves out.”

reading.stem: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: Two neighboring towns quarrel over the use of a valley. One buys its tools from the other; the other depends on a bridge maintained by the first. Even people indifferent to friendship can see a practical reason for negotiating. Breaking off contact would interrupt work on both sides. Trade has certainly not prevented every conflict, and an unequal bargain may itself cause resentment. Still, where both parties expect valuable exchanges to continue, the cost of a quarrel includes tomorrow's lost opportunities. Economic ties can give potential opponents a material interest in preserving peaceful relations.
choices: When Tomorrow's Trade Gives Peace a Practical Ally
The Price of Tools in an Isolated Village
The Bridge That Made Negotiation Unnecessary
How to Remove Mutual Dependence from Markets
Why Every Valuable Bargain Ends in Conflict
evidence: Economic ties can give potential opponents a material interest in preserving peaceful relations.
reading.explanation:
정답 ① · 글의 제목
서로 이익을 얻는 교역은 다투었을 때의 손해도 크게 하여 협상을 유도한다. 교역이 평화를 반드시 보장한다는 주장은 아니다.
근거 “Economic ties can give potential opponents a material interest in preserving peaceful relations.”

reading.stem: 다음 도표의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

title: Students Watching Online Game Tournaments
blocks.note: Case study data for this exercise.

blocks: Students in five clubs reported whether they had watched an online tournament in the preceding week.
choices: For Chess, the figure for April was above the figure for October.
The two bars for Music are 11 percentage points apart.
One of the two figures for Science was below 40.5%, and the other was above it.
For October, the figure for Dance exceeded that for Drama by 4 percentage points.
For April, Drama ranked highest among the five categories.
evidence: Chess: 73, 38
reading.explanation:
정답 ① · 도표 내용 불일치
Chess의 수치는 October 73%, April 38%이므로 두 값의 대소 관계가 반대다.
[지문 근거] “Chess: 73, 38”

reading.stem: John Bowlby에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
blocks: In the household where John Bowlby grew up, much of a young child's care was left to a nanny. At seven he was sent away to boarding school, an experience he later recalled as deeply upsetting. At his father's suggestion he initially read medicine at Cambridge, but his interests increasingly turned toward psychology. His professional attention centered on children's development and the bonds they form with caregivers. For a short period in the 1950s he also advised the World Health Organization on mental health.
choices: 아이와 양육자 사이의 유대에 관심을 기울였다.
어린 시절 돌봄의 많은 부분을 보모가 맡았다.
케임브리지에서 처음부터 심리학을 전공하도록 아버지의 권유를 받았다.
evidence: initially read medicine at Cambridge
reading.explanation:
정답 ⑤ · 내용 불일치
케임브리지에서 처음 선택한 전공은 의학이었고 이후 심리학 쪽으로 관심을 옮겼다.
[지문 근거] “initially read medicine at Cambridge”

reading.stem: Hilltop Pumpkin Dash에 관한 다음 안내문의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

blocks.title: Hilltop Pumpkin Dash
lines: lead
Send a pumpkin rolling down the grassy lane. Stewards will mark the point where it stops, and the longest legal roll wins.
sub
Each contestant has two attempts with the same pumpkin.
sub
Use a pumpkin supplied at the starting point.
sub
Crossing the line before release cancels that attempt.
sub
Children can enter with permission from an adult.
sub
The winners are announced beside the hill at noon.

choices: 호박을 놓기 전에 선을 넘으면 해당 시도가 무효다.
어른의 허락을 받은 어린이가 참가할 수 있다.
evidence: Each contestant has two attempts
reading.explanation:
정답 ② · 안내문 내용 불일치
각자 두 차례 시도할 수 있으므로 기회가 한 번이라는 설명은 틀리다.
[지문 근거] “Each contestant has two attempts”

reading.stem: Jog and Gather에 관한 다음 안내문의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

blocks.title: Jog and Gather
lines: lead
Enjoy a slow jog along the canal and help remove litter. You may walk any section if jogging would make collecting rubbish difficult.
sub
We supply litter pickers, but please bring your own reusable gloves.
sub
Meet at the north end of the bridge.
sub
The shorter route is open to families with children.
sub
Separate glass from the other litter at the finish.
sub
Registration is free and must be completed online.

choices: 재사용 장갑은 참가자가 직접 가져와야 한다.
온라인 등록 시 반드시 참가비를 낸다.
짧은 코스에는 어린이를 동반한 가족이 참가할 수 없다.
도착점에서는 유리와 다른 쓰레기를 한데 넣는다.
evidence: bring your own reusable gloves
reading.explanation:
정답 ① · 안내문 내용 일치
집게와 달리 장갑은 직접 가져와야 한다.
[지문 근거] “bring your own reusable gloves”

reading.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은? [3점]
blocks: At a market, a dealer first shows a customer a lamp ① <u>priced</u> at two hundred dollars. A second lamp now looks cheap by comparison, even if the customer knows little about ② <u>its</u> construction. The first number can continue ③ <u>to shape</u> the discussion long after both people have turned to a different lamp. In a classroom demonstration, a list of prices ④ <u>were</u> handed out before students estimated the cost of an ordinary desk. The exercise helped them notice how readily they relied on figures ⑤ <u>presented</u> earlier.
evidence: a list of prices
reading.explanation:
정답 ④ · 어법
앞의 주어 중심어 list가 단수이므로 수동태 were handed out의 were를 was로 고친다. prices는 전치사 of의 목적어이다.
[지문 근거] “a list of prices”

reading.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은? [3점]
blocks: A person may recall the color of a school bag from the first day of class without recalling the color of every chair. This does not mean the room contained only one ① <u>noticeable</u> object. Remembering is ② <u>indiscriminate</u>, and attention may have rested on the bag because it was new or personally important. If every detail competed equally for later recall, useful information could become harder to ③ <u>retrieve</u>. Letting less relevant details fade may therefore ④ <u>facilitate</u> access to what matters by reducing the competition among memories. In that sense, forgetting can serve a ⑤ <u>practical</u> purpose.
evidence: attention may have rested on the bag
reading.explanation:
정답 ② · 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임
가방에 주의가 집중되어 많은 의자 중 특정 정보만 기억했다는 사례이다. 무차별적이라는 indiscriminate 대신 선택적이라는 selective가 적절하다.
[지문 근거] “attention may have rested on the bag”

reading.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
blocks: A plant-eating animal may find more than enough leaves while still taking in very little salt. If, over many generations, extra salt commonly benefits members of its species, an attraction to a salty taste could guide them toward a useful resource before they learn anything about nutrition. The animal need not measure a shortage or understand what salt does. A physical reward for tasting a certain substance can do the guiding. Thus what appears to be a personal <blank/> may reflect a recurring nutritional problem faced by earlier generations.
evidence: a recurring nutritional problem faced by earlier generations
reading.explanation:
정답 ③ · 빈칸 추론
염분이 적은 먹이를 먹어 온 종에서 짠맛에 끌리는 성향은 반복된 영양상의 필요와 관련될 수 있다. 근거 표현은 “a recurring nutritional problem faced by earlier generations”이다.

reading.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
blocks: An experienced stage manager stops a rehearsal just before a heavy curtain begins to fall unevenly. Asked what warned her, she first says that something simply felt wrong. Later, watching a recording, she notices a small delay between the movement of two ropes. She had encountered a similar delay many times before, although she could not name it quickly enough at rehearsal. Her feeling was immediate, but the information underlying it was external and quite specific. What seemed to come from nowhere was <blank/>. Recognition arrived before a verbal account of it did.
choices: a decision reached after carefully comparing two explanations
proof that reliable judgments do not depend on experience
an instruction silently communicated by another worker
a judgment made from a cue she had not consciously identified
a memory that became useful only after she saw the recording
evidence: Recognition arrived before a verbal account of it did
reading.explanation:
정답 ④ · 빈칸 추론
느낌을 먼저 의식했지만 지연이라는 시각 단서와 경험이 판단을 이끌었다. 녹화 영상을 본 후에야 그 근거를 말로 설명했다. 근거 표현은 “Recognition arrived before a verbal account of it did”이다.

reading.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3점]
blocks: At a coastal weather station moist air blows toward a long mountain ridge. On the seaward slope the rising air cools and some of its water falls as rain. A farmer on the far side may be only a short distance from the coast on a map, yet the air reaching his fields has already lost much of its moisture. The mountain has not created a new ocean or changed the distance to the old one. It has changed <blank/>. Water that was carried toward the interior has fallen before reaching it.
choices: how much ocean moisture is delivered inland
the direction in which rivers on both slopes flow
how much salt each drop of rain contains
which side of the ridge receives more sunlight
the height at which every inland cloud forms
evidence: Water that was carried toward the interior has fallen before reaching it
reading.explanation:
정답 ① · 빈칸 추론
습한 공기가 산을 넘으며 바다 쪽에 비를 내리기 때문에 내륙에 도착할 때 남은 수분량이 달라진다. 근거 표현은 “Water that was carried toward the interior has fallen before reaching it”이다.

reading.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오. [3점]
blocks: At a volunteer library, people used to apologize if they kept a popular book an extra day. Then a very small daily fee was introduced. A borrower who once worried about the next reader could now regard an extra week as an inexpensive purchase. Removing the charge later did not immediately restore the old feeling of obligation. The problem was not that members could no longer afford books. The fee had <blank/>. By placing a price beside the delay, it had turned a question of consideration into a question of cost.
choices: restored the value of the volunteer's unpaid work
ensured that long delays were no longer permitted
changed the meaning that borrowers gave to being late
increased the inconvenience suffered by each late borrower
made borrowers feel personally closer to waiting readers
evidence: turned a question of consideration into a question of cost
reading.explanation:
정답 ③ · 빈칸 추론
소액 요금으로 인해 양해를 구할 위반이 값을 내고 살 수 있는 선택으로 해석되었다. 금액보다 규범의 의미 변화가 핵심이다. 근거 표현은 “turned a question of consideration into a question of cost”이다.

reading.stem: 다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
blocks: A traditional account pictures a good decision maker as a person who can reason accurately in private. ① Some meeting rooms place name cards on the table so that visitors can find their assigned seats. ② According to this account, an error in judgment can be traced to some weakness in the individual's calculation. ③ A teacher accepting the account would therefore ask each pupil to practice weighing evidence more carefully. ④ The solution follows from the premise: improving the thinker is expected to improve the decision. ⑤ Even a familiar group mistake would, on this view, be approached by training the members one at a time.
evidence: improving the thinker is expected to improve the decision
reading.explanation:
정답 ① · 흐름과 무관한 문장
다른 문장은 개인 추론 능력을 기르면 의사결정을 개선할 수 있다는 하나의 관점을 전개한다. 회의장 이름표는 그 관점과 관계가 없다. 근거 표현은 “improving the thinker is expected to improve the decision”이다.

reading.stem: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: A museum presents two imaginary markets. In both, a shop sells a powder that looks like expensive ground coffee but is made from a cheaper root.
In the first market an inspector can demand that the shop label its goods accurately. She regards the seller, who mixed the powder, as the person best placed to prevent a misunderstanding.

Visitors who step between the two displays encounter the same product and entirely different risks. The difference comes from the way responsibility for discovering the substitution has been distributed.
Across the dividing line, an inspector has no such power. Buyers there are told to examine what they purchase, even though few could recognize the mixture by sight.
evidence: Across the dividing line
reading.explanation:
정답 ① · 글의 순서 (2점)
(A) - (C) - (B)의 순서이다. 첫 번째 시장에서 판매자가 표시 책임을 지고, 두 번째 시장에서 구매자가 책임을 지는 차이를 제시한 뒤 같은 제품의 위험이 달라지는 이유를 설명한다.
[지문 근거] “Across the dividing line”

reading.stem: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은? [3점]
blocks: A report on a damaged reef included photographs taken immediately after a period of unusually warm water. Most showed pale coral and very little animal activity.
A difference of this kind would not erase the damage caused by warming. It could, however, suggest a local practice worth testing while broader efforts to limit the warming continue.
The photographs correctly recorded a serious loss. Nevertheless, a diver who returned over several years saw small patches recover while nearby patches remained almost bare.
That uneven recovery led her to compare the sites. One question was whether local fishing practices had left more plant-eating fish in the places where young corals survived.
evidence: That uneven recovery
reading.explanation:
정답 ③ · 글의 순서 (3점)
(B) - (C) - (A)의 순서이다. 손상 사진 이후 일부 구역에서만 회복되는 현상을 관찰하고, 이를 구역별 관리 차이와 연결해 조사한 뒤 제한적인 실천 가능성을 제시한다.
[지문 근거] “That uneven recovery”

reading.stem: 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
blocks: After half an hour, several listeners began to find its sharp brightness tiring.

A shop tested two sets of headphones by playing the same violin recording for a few seconds through each. ( ① ) Listeners often selected the pair with extra emphasis on high notes, describing the recording as wonderfully clear. ( ② ) The staff wondered whether the same pair would be preferred during a complete concert. ( ③ ) This change of preference mattered because most customers planned to wear the headphones for far longer than a brief demonstration. ( ④ ) The shop consequently added a longer listening session to its comparison procedure. ( ⑤ ) The first impression had been genuine, but it answered a question about an interval much shorter than the one the customers cared about.
evidence: This change of preference
reading.explanation:
정답 ③ · 문장 삽입 (2점)
긴 감상에서도 같은 기기를 선호할지 묻고, 피로 때문에 선호가 바뀐 결과를 제시한 뒤 그 변화의 의미를 설명한다.
[지문 근거] “This change of preference”

reading.stem: 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은? [3점]
blocks: The sunlit plant can direct more of its limited resources to developing broad leaves instead.

Two trays of seedlings came from the same packet. One was placed by a sunny window; the other was kept in a dark cupboard for a short period. ( ① ) Despite their shared origin, the seedlings in the cupboard grew surprisingly long, thin stems. ( ② ) A seedling under fallen leaves might reach daylight sooner by spending stored energy on such rapid extension. ( ③ ) But once light is available, pouring the same share of its reserves into a long stem would serve less purpose. ( ④ ) These larger light-catching surfaces allow it to obtain energy for further growth. ( ⑤ ) The contrast between the trays can thus represent two different uses of the same initial budget.
evidence: These larger light-catching surfaces
reading.explanation:
정답 ④ · 문장 삽입 (3점)
어두운 곳의 줄기 신장과 대비하여 밝은 곳의 넓은 잎 발달을 소개해야 These larger light-catching surfaces가 무엇인지 분명해진다.

reading.stem: 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
blocks: At a school market game, everyone inspected the same chart showing the price of grain. Half the class represented growers, who gained points if the price rose. The others represented millers, who gained points if it fell. Both groups could also earn points for an accurate forecast, so neither had a reason to give a deliberately false prediction. Nevertheless, the growers generally expected higher prices than the millers did. The chart had never changed; what differed was which outcome each group wanted. Wishing for a result had apparently colored an attempt to judge it accurately.
Despite (A) price information, the roles assigned to forecasters can (B) their estimates toward the result each would welcome.
evidence: The chart had never changed
which outcome each group wanted
reading.explanation:
정답 ① · 요약문 완성 (2점)
같은 도표와 정확성 보상이 주어져도 집단별 유리한 결과가 달라 예측이 원하는 방향으로 기울었다.
[지문 근거] “The chart had never changed” / “which outcome each group wanted”

41-42.head: [41~42] 다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오.
blocks: An unfamiliar sound in an empty house is only a sound until someone imagines a loose shutter or a visitor at the door. The little story connects a present cue to an expected (a) <u>consequence</u>. That connection permits action before the source of the sound is certain. It also creates a danger. After settling on the visitor story, a listener may (b) <u>notice</u> a scratch near the lock and ignore the moving shutter. The story has both guided attention and (c) <u>filtered</u> it. A bare list of scratches, sounds and movements would not by itself tell the listener what to check first. Yet the first useful story should remain (d) <u>immune</u> to revision: the listener ought to replace it if a test shows that wind produces exactly the same noise. The skill is not to live without stories, but to keep the link between a story and an observation (e) <u>open</u> to correction.

43-45.head: [43~45] 다음 글을 읽고, 물음에 답하시오.
blocks: On a rainy evening Inez noticed a woman outside the station holding a damp piece of cardboard. Thinking it was a sign asking for money, Inez took a coin from (a) <u>her</u> coat. The woman shook her head and pointed to a line of print that the rain had almost erased.

The bus came before Inez had finished drying (b) <u>her</u> glasses. The woman boarded, then called back the name of a bakery that sold hot rolls near the station. On the walk home Inez bought one and thought how nearly (c) <u>she</u> had missed that conversation.

Inez bent closer. The cardboard was a bus timetable, and the woman wanted to know when the last bus left. Inez put away (d) <u>her</u> coin and read the time aloud. There were six minutes left and the stop was across the square.

The woman pulled an umbrella from (e) <u>her</u> bag and held it over both their heads. They reached the stop together. While they waited, Inez admitted that she had misunderstood the cardboard; the woman laughed and offered her the handle so she could dry her glasses.
